core_obligations: Identify the morphism and the first square (proof lines 7953-7964): f_qc comes from the continuous functor Z/Y |-> Z x_Y X/X, and the left-hand square of topoi commutes because the corresponding continuous functors compose correctly.
Get the second square (proof lines 7965-7968): the right-hand square commutes because the left one does, together with part (5) of the collected Zariski comparison lemma.

Reduce the proper case to a Zariski statement (proof lines 7969-7976): to show that a_Y^{-1}f_*F -> f_qc,*a_X^{-1}F is an isomorphism it suffices to show that pi_Y^{-1}f_*F = epsilon_{Y,*}a_Y^{-1}f_*F -> epsilon_{Y,*}f_qc,*a_X^{-1}F = f_{Zar,*}epsilon_{X,*}a_X^{-1}F = f_{Zar,*}pi_X^{-1}F is an isomorphism.
Conclude (proof lines 7977-7983): that last isomorphism is part (7a) of the collected Zariski comparison lemma, so the push-pull statement for a proper f follows.
proof_roadmap: Check the two commutative diagrams from the composition of the underlying continuous functors and the collected Zariski properties.
Reduce the proper push-pull identity to a Zariski statement by applying epsilon_{Y,*} to both sides.
Quote the collected Zariski comparison statement to finish.
difficulty_reason: The lemma establishes the commutativity of the comparison diagrams for a morphism of LC_qc and, for proper f, the push-pull identity a_Y^{-1}f_* = f_qc,*a_X^{-1} (statement lines 7925-7950). The proof (proof lines 7952-7983) identifies f_qc through relocalisation, derives the two diagrams from the composition of continuous functors and the collected Zariski comparison properties, reduces the push-pull identity to a Zariski statement after applying epsilon_{Y,*}, and quotes part (7a) of the collected statements. H2: one identification and one reduction, written out.
